messages.subject: Log-likelihood function for constant CJS model with chi-term
parts:
Hello! I am struggling writting down the log-likelihood function for the basic CJS model with constant parameters. The results for the frequentist and the Bayesian approach (in m-array formulation for the later) do not match, I do not know where the problem is, but I am sure the problem is somewhere in the function below. Any help would be really appreciated...

f: first time seen
l: last time seen

loglik <- function(theta, nind, n.occasions,data,f,l){
 
  phi <- array(0,n.occasions-1)
  p <- array(0,(n.occasions-1))
  temp1 <- matrix(0,nrow=nind, ncol=n.occasions)
  temp2 <- c()
  loglik <- c()
  lik <- array(0,nind)
  chi <- array(1,dim=c(nind,n.occasions))
 
  # Define the parameters to be constant
  for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)) {
    p[t+1] <- 1/(1+exp(-theta[1]))
    phi[t] <- 1/(1+exp(-theta[2]))
  }
 
  for (i in 1:nind){
    lik[i] <- 0
    if (f[i]!=l[i]){
      for (j in f[i]:(l[i]-1)){
        temp1[i,j] <- log(phi[j])
        temp2[i] <- sum(temp1[i,f[i]:(l[i]-1)])
      }
      lik[i] <- lik[i] + temp2[i]
   
      for (j in f[i]:(l[i]-1)){
        lik[i] <- lik[i] + data[i,j+1]*log(p[j+1]) + (1-data[i,j+1])*log(1-p[j+1])
      }
    }

  # To calculate the probability of not being observed
    if (l[i] < n.occasions){
      chi[i,n.occasions] <- 1
      for (j in (n.occasions-1):l[i]){
        chi[i,j] <- 1 - phi[j]*(1-(1-p[[j+1]])*chi[i,j+1])
      }
    }
 
    lik[i] <- lik[i] + sum(log(chi[i,]))
  } # i
 
  loglik <- -sum(lik) # the function "optim" return the minimum by default
  return(loglik)
}
